page.layout: Two woodcut medallion portraits centred at top; below them one column of running text with two paragraphs (the first a biography of Amurathes, the second a short entry on Solimanus); full width. Printed running head at top with page number at left.

main_text.p: AMVRATHES huius nominis primus, Orchanis filius, mortuo patre, apud Turcas imperat anno mundi 5311. à Christo nato 1349. Is auitam paternámque felicitatem æmulatus eft: at vero in Caramanum auum maternum non minus infestus quàm pater fuit, qui socerum occiso eius filio adolescente non minima Ciliciæ parte exuerat. Cæterùm à Constantinopolitano Imperatore Ioanne Palæologo solicitatus Amurathes 12000. Turcarum ei in auxilium mittit: idque initium ac origo ruinæ imperij Constantinopolitani fuit. Nam Europeis opibus illectus Amurathes, opis denuo adferendæ simulatione, potiundæ tamen Græciæ animo, Genuensium nauibus vsus Amurathes, Thurcarum 60000. in Græciam transportat: Hellespontum ad Abydum superat: Callipolim cum aliis oppidis occupat: in ipsum quoque Imperatorem inexpectato grauem impetum facit. Postea Seruiam, Bulgariamque ingressus, Lazarum Seruiæ, & Marcum Bulgariæ principes, cum paratissimis copiis ei occurentes, ingenti cæde profligat, prius occupata Adrianopoli: sed Lazaro cæso, mox à feruo in domini vindictam Amurathes occiditur, anno regni 23. Vide Egna.lib.2. Pau.Io.& Christop.Richerium de rebus Turcarum lib.1.

SOLIMANVS Amurathis filius, patri in imperio succedens, confestim hæreditariæ dignitati eripitur, atque per insidias occiditur à fratre æmulo Baiazete: quamobrem à nonnullis inter Turcicos Imperatores minimè annumeratur. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits: left labelled "THES TVRC R." and "AMVRA"; right labelled "SOLIMANVS R." and "AMVRAT". Lower-left faint show-through only; not transcribed. Several words in the text are set in a slightly lighter or uneven inking and were read with care; "Amurathes" in the first paragraph and the numerals 5311, 12000, 60000 and 23 are copied as printed (the printed numerals in the original read "5 3 11", "1 2 0 0 0", "6 0 0 0 0" and "2 3"). Where the scan is faint the reading is uncertain but no [?] markers were required.
